points.why: It sees the erosion as real, persistent forces rather than defiance and notes that silence wasn't buy-in, but it never frames this as a process correcting toward an unstated goal.
There is no loop of state, implicit target, gap and correction; it only says the pressure decays as exceptions arrive.
It asks engineers whether they get focus time, not the people booking Wednesday meetings what they're protecting, and it doesn't treat 'nobody knows' as a finding.

Async alternatives, accommodating real demands and fewer meetings overall point the right way, but most fixes add enforcement, and it never says a stronger message leaves the underlying target untouched.

pitfalls.why: It argues against a message-only re-announcement and blames no bookers; it points at leadership's own exceptions instead.

notes: Leaning on approvers, exception counts and an owner with authority to say no pushes harder on the state without moving the target, which risks the same drift through workarounds.
